faqs.q: How do I know if my Irvington leak is a flashing problem or a shingle problem?

runs.v: A leak at a wall intersection, chimney, dormer, skylight, or valley is almost always a flashing failure. A shingle leak shows mid-plane, where a shingle is missing, cracked, or lifted.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for flashing repair in Irvington?

runs.v: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in NJ? Not on a detached one- or two-family home, where roof covering repair or replacement, flashing included, is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 of the NJ Uniform Construction Code. Major flashing repairs or replacements on commercial, multi-family, or attached buildings can need a permit under the 25% rule above, so confirm with the Irvington construction office.

faqs.q: Does flashing repair on an Irvington historic home need extra approval?

runs.v: It can. A locally designated landmark or historic-district property can need extra review, so confirm with the Irvington construction office before work begins. National Register listing alone places no restriction on a private owner, per the National Park Service.

faqs.q: Why does my Irvington chimney leak after previous repairs?

runs.v: Chimney leaks that return usually mean the last repair relied on sealant, which dries and cracks over deteriorated metal or eroded mortar, per GAF technical guidance. A lasting repair rebuilds the two-part base-and-counter flashing.

faqs.q: Should flashing be replaced when I get a new roof in Irvington?

runs.v: Yes. Reused flashing is a common source of premature leaks on a new roof, so step, chimney, and valley flashing, drip edge, and vent-pipe boots are replaced at a full roof replacement.
